title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not in Grothendieck's hand. It is page 10 of a typed English manuscript, and its style and content match Dennis Sullivan's exposition of 'non-abelian periods' from around 1973–75: the Tokyo 'Differential forms and the topology of manifolds' paper and the material that became 'Infinitesimal computations in topology'. Grothendieck kept it among his notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The neighbouring Grothendieck pages develop a notion of differential k-algebra C* on a topos with only partially defined products (one factor must be a cocycle). That reads as an attempt to transpose Sullivan's commutative-cochain approach to arbitrary coefficient rings.

Mathematics of the page, in modern terms:
1. H is the real Heisenberg group of unipotent upper-triangular 3×3 matrices.
2. Its left-invariant 1-forms are dx, dy and a third form θ = dz ± x dy, with dθ = ±dx∧dy.
3. So the Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra of its Lie algebra is the Sullivan minimal algebra Λ(x1, x2, y), with |x_i| = |y| = 1, d x_i = 0 and dy = x1 x2.
4. Take a manifold M with closed 1-forms ω1, ω2 whose cup product is exact, ω1∧ω2 = dη.
5. Integrating along paths from a base point p (iterated integrals in Chen's sense) gives a map φ: M → H/Γ. This is a de Rham realisation of a morphism of dg algebras Λ(x1, x2, y) → Ω*(M).
6. Γ is the image of π1 modulo the third term of its lower central series, modulo torsion. This is the second nilpotent quotient, a lattice in H. Lattices of the form {(n, m, ℓ/k)} with k fixed are exactly the Heisenberg lattices up to isomorphism.
7. Composing with the abelianisation H/Γ → T² gives the Albanese/Jacobian (Abel–Jacobi) map defined by ω1, ω2. Thus φ is a 'nilpotent' or 'higher Albanese' map.
8. The page then asserts generalisations: to all nilpotent quotients Γ_k of π1 (the Malcev completion), and to nilpotent quotients of higher homotopy groups as π1-modules. In the simply connected case this gives a complete set of real periods for the higher homotopy groups. That is Sullivan's theorem that the minimal model computes Hom(π_*, R).
errors: The typed matrices show bottom-right entry 0; it should be 1 for unipotent matrices. This is a typo in the original typescript.

Sign convention: with the standard product of upper-triangular matrices, the left-invariant form is dz − x dy (right-invariant: dz − y dx). 'dz + x dy' requires a different parametrisation. This is harmless.

Landing in the compact quotient H/Γ requires ω1, ω2 to be integral, and η to be chosen so that its periods lie in (1/k)Z. Otherwise the map goes to H modulo the period group, which need not be discrete. 'In this case' implicitly assumes b1 = 2, i.e. that π1/Γ3 mod torsion is exactly a Heisenberg lattice; in general it is a larger nilpotent lattice.
'quotents' is a typo for 'quotients' in the original.

ideas.what: Minimal model Λ(x1, x2, y), dy = x1x2, identified with the left-invariant forms on the Heisenberg group
ideas.modern_name: Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra / Sullivan minimal model of a nilmanifold (Nomizu theorem)

ideas.what: Integrating forms along paths to get a map M → H/Γ realising a Massey-type relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1975/77), K.-T. Chen; later Hain ('higher Albanese manifolds')

ideas.what: Real periods of the nilpotent quotients of π1 and of the higher homotopy groups via minimal models
ideas.modern_name: Malcev completion / rational homotopy via the minimal model; Hom(π_*, R) from the indecomposables

missed.claim: Archival/historical point only: the folder for Grothendieck's 1976 divided-power de Rham talk contains a typescript page of Sullivan's work on non-abelian periods. It sits next to Grothendieck's own drafts of 'differential algebras with partial products' on a topos. This documents that he read Sullivan's rational-homotopy de Rham theory while seeking an integral or torsion analogue. The mathematics on this page is Sullivan's and is published.
missed.quote: These non-abelian periods generalize to the higher nilpotent quotents {Γ_k} of π1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to the history of integral and p-adic homotopy-via-cochains (Mandell's E∞ theorem, divided-power and crystalline approaches). It shows an early Grothendieck–Sullivan link that is not usually mentioned.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript by another author (Sullivan-style exposition) containing standard, published material. The only interest is archival: evidence of Grothendieck's reading in connection with his divided-power de Rham project.
transcription_corrections: This page is a typed English manuscript (page number 10, archive stamp 350), not Grothendieck's handwriting.
The bottom-right matrix entries are typed as 0 in the original; mathematically they should be 1.
